title: METAR & TAF: Read Weather Like a Dispatcher
hook: KDEN 271753Z 33015G25KT... gibberish, or a go/no-go answer?

scenes.narration: Phone out in the hangar. The METAR reads: wind three-three-zero at fifteen gusting two-five, ten miles, scattered at four thousand... temp twelve, dew point eleven. Sun's setting, kid. See the trap yet?
Temp twelve, dew point eleven, sun going down. What's this field doing in two hours? Commit.
Fog. One degree of spread at sunset means saturation is one degree of cooling away — the fog is already filing its flight plan. That's the read a dispatcher makes in three seconds.
The format never changes: station, Zulu time, wind, visibility, weather, clouds, temp-dew, altimeter. Why no vowels? Teletype charged by the character, eighty years ago. Nobody's put them back.

The TAF is the forecast — twenty-four to thirty hours, five miles around the field. F M means a hard switch. TEMPO means it'll misbehave, then apologize. And a ceiling is BROKEN or OVERCAST — scattered doesn't count.
Eyes off the screen. What counts as a ceiling — and what does a closing temp-dew spread promise? Out loud.
METAR is now. TAF is later. Broken or overcast makes a ceiling. And when temp meets dew point, be on the ground watching it happen.
From the takeoff-minimums lesson — Part ninety-one required takeoff minimums. What are they? Careful.
A C zero zero dash forty-five H — Aviation Weather Services. All the decoder rings.

quiz.question: Temperature 12°C, dew point 11°C, sun setting. Expect:
quiz.explanation: A small, closing temp/dew point spread near sunset is the classic fog setup — saturation is one degree of cooling away.

quiz.question: Which cloud reports constitute a ceiling?
quiz.explanation: A ceiling is the lowest broken or overcast layer, or vertical visibility into an obscuration. Scattered doesn't count.

quiz.question: In a TAF, "FM1500" means:
choices: A rapid, lasting change to new conditions beginning at 1500Z
quiz.explanation: FM (FROM) groups signal a fast, permanent change to the new conditions at that Zulu time; TEMPO covers temporary fluctuations.
